questions.qtext: The degree sequence of a simple graph is the sequence of the degree of the nodes in the graph in decreasing order. Which of the following sequence can be the degree sequence of any graph?
questions.solution:
(a, b)
Using Havell-Hakimi algorithm:
(i) Remove top node of the sequence.
(ii) Substract 1 from as many nodes in remaining sequence as the degree of top node that was removed.
(iii) Rearrange the sequence in non-increasing order.
(iv) Check if result sequence is a graph.
(v) Proceed again step (i)
If the given sequence is not a graph. We will see a violation in step (iv). Such as presence of negative degrees in the sequence. Otherwise the algorithm will bottom out with a degree sequence consisting of only even number of 1’s and any number of 0’s.

questions.qtext: Let (G, *) be a group such that Ο(G) = 8. Where Ο(G) denotes the order of the group. Which of the following is true?

options.text: There exist no element a in G whose order is 6.
There exist an element a in G whose order is 4.
There exist more than one element in G whose order is 1.

questions.solution:
(a)
Let G be a finite group of order k then every element of G will have order m such that k and m = 0
(a) True
8 mod 6 = 2
(b) False
8 mod 4 = 0 but it not necessary that there must exist an element with order 4.
(c) False
There must exist only 1 identity element in a group.
